attempts.sql:
SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.files f ON s.file_id = f.file_id
WHERE f.is_test = FALSE
  AND s.kind = 'class'
  AND s.symbol_id IN (
    SELECT cb.base_symbol_id
    FROM code.class_bases cb
    WHERE cb.base_name = 'object'
  )
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC;

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: The query identifies classes by filtering for symbols with kind='class' in non-test files. It then restricts to classes that directly inherit from 'object' (i.e., not abstract base classes with further inheritance), ensuring only methods defined directly in the class body are counted via the class_bases view. Grouping by symbol_id and counting method definitions yields the per-class method totals, which are filtered to >=20 and ordered as requested.
sql:
SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.files f ON s.file_id = f.file_id
WHERE f.is_test = FALSE
  AND s.kind = 'class'
  AND s.symbol_id IN (
    SELECT cb.base_symbol_id
    FROM code.class_bases cb
    WHERE cb.base_name = 'object'
  )
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC;
